questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Obstinate
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.
Obstinate
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Stubborn.

Key Points

  • The word "Obstinate" means stubbornly refusing to change one's opinion or chosen course of action, despite attempts to persuade one to do so. (हठी)
    • Example: Despite many arguments, he remained obstinate in his decision to not sell the house.
  • "Stubborn" refers to having or showing dogged determination not to change one's attitude or position on something, especially in spite of good arguments or reasons to do so. (जिद्दी)
    • Example: The stubborn child refused to eat his vegetables.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Stubborn.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Obedient (आज्ञाकारी): Complying or willing to comply with orders or requests; submissive to another's will.
    • Example: The obedient dog sat quietly by his owner's side.
  • Adaptive (अनुकूलनीय): Able to adjust to new conditions.
    • Example: She is highly adaptive and can handle any situation.
  • Submissive (आज्ञाकारी): Ready to conform to the authority or will of others; meekly obedient or passive.
    • Example: The submissive employee never questioned his boss's decisions.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Left out in the cold
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Left out in the cold
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 3.

Key Points

  • The phrase "Left out in the cold" means to be ignored or excluded from something. (अनदेखा करना या किसी चीज से बाहर रखना)
    • Example: When the project was handed out, she felt left out in the cold as she wasn't given any significant tasks.
  • "Ignored" means to deliberately pay no attention to someone or something. (अनदेखा करना)
    • Example: He ignored all the warnings and went ahead with his plan.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • To go underground (भूमिगत हो जाना): To go into hiding or to become secretive.
    • Example: After the scandal, he decided to go underground to avoid the media.
  • To be in hiding (छिपा हुआ होना): To stay in a place where you cannot be found.
    • Example: The fugitive was in hiding for several months before he was captured.
  • To be extremely negative (अत्यंत नकारात्मक होना): To have a very pessimistic outlook or attitude.
    • Example: His comments about the project were extremely negative and unhelpful.

questions.question: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence. P. and has also created a wide gap between them Q. laid too much stress on R. teachers and students S. online mode of education has
questions.questionHtml:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.
P. and has also created a wide gap between them
Q. laid too much stress on
R. teachers and students
S. online mode of education has
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option (3) i.e. SQRP
Key Points
  • The sentence logically starts with "Online mode of education has," which is correctly indicated by part (S).
  • Following this, "laid too much stress on" (Q) continues the phrase, explaining what the online education mode has done.
  • The next part, "teachers and students" (R) specifies who is affected by the stress mentioned.
  • Ending with, "and has also created a wide gap between them" (P) completes the sentence by describing the consequence of the stress.
Therefore, the correct answer is SQRP.
Additional Information
  • Option 1 (SRPQ): This option places "a wide gap between them" before mentioning who is affected, disrupting the logical flow.
  • Option 2 (RQPS): This option starts with "teachers and students," which does not complete a thought without specifying what the online mode of education has done.
  • Option 4 (PSQR): This option starts with "and has also created a wide gap between them," without providing context for what has created the gap.

questions.question: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A thing that can be easily carried by hands
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.
A thing that can be easily carried by hands
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Portable.

Key Points

  • The word "thing" means an object that one need not, cannot, or does not wish to give a specific name to. (वस्तु)
    • Example: This thing is very useful for our project.
  • "Carried" refers to support and move (someone or something) from one place to another. (ले जाना)
    • Example: He carried the heavy box to the car.
  • "Portable" means something that can be easily carried by hands. (पोर्टेबल)
    • Example: The portable speaker is easy to carry around.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Portable.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Export (निर्यात): To send goods or services to another country for sale.
    • Example: The company exports its products to various countries around the world.
  • Import (आयात): To bring goods or services into a country from abroad for sale.
    • Example: We import coffee beans from Brazil.
  • Potable (पेय): Safe to drink; drinkable.
    • Example: The water from the well is potable.

questions.question: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence. O. want P. movie tonight Q. do you R. to watch S. the
questions.questionHtml:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.
O. want
P. movie tonight
Q. do you
R. to watch
S. the
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option (2) i.e. QORSP
Key Points
  • The sentence logically starts with "Do you," which is correctly indicated by part (Q).
  • Following this, "want" (O) continues the sentence, as it naturally follows "do you."
  • The next part "to watch" (R) specifies the action you want to do.
  • The part "the" (S) introduces the object of the sentence.
  • Ending with "movie tonight" (P) completes the thought by specifying what is to be watched.
Therefore, the correct answer is QORSP.
Additional Information
  • Option 1 (RSPQO): This option starts with "to watch," which does not form a complete question without context from the beginning.
  • Option 3 (OSQPR): This option starts with "want," which does not form a grammatical question.
  • Option 4 (OSPQR): This option starts with "want," which does not form a grammatical question.

questions.question: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence. A. Only for themselves B. Is full of C. People who live D. The world
questions.questionHtml:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.
A. Only for themselves
B. Is full of
C. People who live
D. The world
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option (4) i.e. DBCA
Key Points
  • The sentence logically starts with "The world," which is correctly indicated by part (D).
  • Following this, "is full of" (B) continues the sentence, explaining the state of the world.
  • Next, "people who live" (C) specifies the kind of people filling up the world.
  • Ending with "only for themselves" (A) completes the sentence by describing the nature of those people.
Therefore, the correct answer is DBCA.
Additional Information
  • Option 1 (BCAD): This option starts with "is full of," which leaves the sentence without a subject at the beginning.
  • Option 2 (ABCD): This option starts with "only for themselves," which does not provide context or a clear subject initially.
  • Option 3 (DBAC): This option places "only for themselves" before "people who live," which makes the sentence structure awkward and unclear.

questions.question: Select the option that correctly expresses the given sentence in passive voice. Mr. Amar refused him admittance.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that correctly expresses the given sentence in passive voice.
Mr. Amar refused him admittance.

options.text: Admittance will be refused to him by Mr. Amar.
options.html: Admittance will be refused to him by Mr. Amar.

options.text: Admittance shall be refused to him by Mr. Amar.
options.html: Admittance shall be refused to him by Mr. Amar.

options.text: Admittance would be refused to him by Mr. Amar.
options.html: Admittance would be refused to him by Mr. Amar.

options.text: Admittance was refused to him by Mr. Amar.
options.html: Admittance was refused to him by Mr. Amar.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 4.
 
Key Points
  • Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
  • In the active voice, the sentence is: "Mr. Amar refused him admittance."
  • To convert to passive voice: Place the object "admittance" at the beginning.
  • Change the active verb form "refused" to "was refused" (past simple passive).
  • Add the preposition "to" followed by the indirect object "him" and the preposition "by" followed by the original subject "Mr. Amar."
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.
 
Correct Sentence: "Admittance was refused to him by Mr. Amar."
 
Additional Information
  • Option 1: "Admittance will be refused to him by Mr. Amar." – Incorrect tense (future simple passive).
  • Option 2: "Admittance shall be refused to him by Mr. Amar." – Incorrect use of modal verb "shall."
  • Option 3: "Admittance would be refused to him by Mr. Amar." – Incorrect tense (conditional passive).

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Break the ice
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Break the ice

options.text: Ill-feeling carried by a person over a period of time
options.html: Ill-feeling carried by a person over a period of time

options.text: To say or do something that makes people feel more relaxed, especially at the beginning of a meeting, party
options.html: To say or do something that makes people feel more relaxed, especially at the beginning of a meeting, party

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 4.

Key Points

  • The idiom "Break the ice" means to say or do something that makes people feel more relaxed, especially at the beginning of a meeting, party, etc. (बातचीत की शुरुआत करना)
    • Example: He told a joke to break the ice at the start of the meeting.
  • "Break the ice" is often used in social or business situations to ease tension or awkwardness among people.
    • Example: The host's warm smile and friendly greeting helped to break the ice with the new guests.
  • Hence, the idiom "Break the ice" is best explained by Option 4.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Nervousness before a performance (प्रदर्शन से पहले घबराहट): The feeling of anxiety or tension before performing in front of an audience.
    • Example: She felt a lot of nervousness before her first stage performance.
  • Ill-feeling carried by a person over a period of time (लंबे समय तक व्यक्ति द्वारा धारण की गई बुरी भावना): Sustained resentment or bitterness.
    • Example: He carried an ill-feeling toward his colleague for years after the incident.
  • Respect for someone's achievements (किसी की उपलब्धियों के लिए सम्मान): Appreciation or admiration for someone's accomplishments.
    • Example: We all have great respect for her remarkable achievements in the field of science.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate homophone to fill in the blank. The summer was _____ hot this year.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate homophone to fill in the blank.
The summer was _____ hot this year.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'too'.
Key Points
  • The word "too" means to a higher degree than is desirable, permissible, or possible; excessively. (अत्यधिक)
  • In the sentence, "too hot" indicates that the heat was excessive or more than usual.
  • The other options: "tow," "two," and "to" do not fit the context as appropriately.

Therefore, the correct answer is 'Option 4'.

Complete Sentence: The summer was too hot this year.

Additional Information
  • Tow (खींचना): means to pull along with a rope or chain.
  • Two (दो): refers to the number 2.
  • To (की और से, तक): is a preposition used to indicate the direction towards a place, person, or position.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the bracketed word in the following sentence to fill in the blank. The mothers, who suffer from postpartum depression, feel ______ by their children. (vexed)

  • The word "vexed" means feeling annoyed, frustrated, or worried. (परेशान)
    • Example: She was vexed by the constant noise coming from the construction site.
  • "Annoyed" refers to feeling slightly angry or irritated. (चिढ़)
    • Example: He was annoyed by the repeated interruptions during his presentation.
  • Hence, we can infer that the synonym of 'vexed' is 'annoyed'.

questions.question: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. I have sing ‘Let It Go’ before a crowd of thousands of people.
questions.questionHtml:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.
I have sing ‘Let It Go’ before a crowd of thousands of people.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 3.
 
Key Points
  • The primary issue in the sentence is the incorrect usage of the verb "sing" instead of "sung."
  • The present perfect tense ("I have...") requires the past participle form of the verb.
  • The correct phrase should be "I have sung," ensuring grammatical accuracy.
  • Thus, the error is located in Option 3 of the sentence.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.
 
Correct Sentence: "I have sung ‘Let It Go’ before a crowd of thousands of people."

questions.question: In the question, four alternatives are given for the underlined word in the sentence. Choose the alternative which best expresses the opposite meaning of the word. It was as if the newer hybrids had an insatiable appetite for chemicals.
questions.questionHtml:
In the question, four alternatives are given for the underlined word in the sentence. Choose the alternative which best expresses the opposite meaning of the word.
It was as if the newer hybrids had an insatiable appetite for chemicals.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Satisfiable.

Key Points

  • The word "insatiable" means having an appetite or desire that cannot be satisfied. (अतृप्त)
    • Example: His insatiable thirst for knowledge led him to read every book in the library.
  • "Satisfiable" refers to something that can be satisfied or fulfilled. (संतोषजनक)
    • Example: The demands of the workers were reasonable and satisfiable by the management.
  • Hence, we can infer that the opposite of 'insatiable' is 'satisfiable'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Satisfiable.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Urgent (तत्काल ): Requiring immediate action or attention.
    • Example: The patient needs urgent medical care.
  • Curbed (नियंत्रित): Restrained or kept in check.
    • Example: The government has curbed the use of plastic bags to protect the environment.
  • Pressing (महत्वपूर्ण): Requiring immediate attention; urgent.
    • Example: There are pressing issues that need to be addressed immediately.

Lady Stranleigh continued to smile at him brilliantly.

questions.question: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice. Trigonometry has been taught by him for donkey's years.

Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.
Trigonometry has been taught by him for donkey's years.

options.text: He had been teaching trigonometry for donkey's years.
options.html: He had been teaching trigonometry for donkey's years.

options.text: He has been trigonometry teaching for donkey's years.

options.text: He has taught trigonometry for donkey's years.
options.html: He has taught trigonometry for donkey's years.

questions.solution:

Key Points
  • Active voice structure: The subject of the passive voice sentence becomes the object of the active voice sentence.
  • In the passive voice, the sentence is: "Trigonometry has been taught by him for donkey's years.."

  • Ensure the time phrase "for donkey's years" remains at the end of the sentence for clarity.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.
 
Correct Sentence: He has taught trigonometry for donkey's years.
 
Additional Information
  • Option 1: "He had been teaching trigonometry for donkey's years." – Incorrect tense (past perfect continuous).
  • Option 2: "He has been trigonometry teaching for donkey's years." – Incorrect word order.
  • Option 3: "He is teaching trigonometry for donkey's years." – Incorrect tense (present continuous).

questions.question: Choose the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.

  • Effect (प्रभाव डालना): Means to bring about a change, but is not commonly used in the phrase "effect out."

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'intricate'.
 
Key Points
  • The passage conveys the complexity and detail involved in mastering the art of singing.
  • 'Intricate' is the most appropriate word to describe a highly refined and complex art form.
  • Other options like 'uncomplicated,' 'uniform,' and 'mixed' are less suitable in this context.
Therefore, the correct answer is 'Option 4'.
 
Additional Information
  • Uncomplicated (सरल): Means simple and easy to do, which contradicts the idea of complexity in the art form.
  • Uniform (समरूप): Means consistent and not varying, which does not imply complexity or refinement.
  • Mixed (मिश्रित): Means combined from different sources, which does not describe the refined and detailed nature needed to be conveyed.
